sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Greensboro, NC?
sections.html:
A Greensboro owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash purchase from a buyer who takes the house in its current condition. The right path depends on how much repair work the house needs, how soon you must close, and whether anyone else holds a claim on the title.

Greensboro sits in Guilford County, the county that appraises and bills property here. The city runs its own permit, zoning and code compliance offices, so a seller with open violations or unfinished work should check those records before accepting any offer. The city site lists a code compliance case lookup and a building permit portal for that purpose.

  • Agent listing: the widest buyer pool, but you carry repairs, showings and the wait for a buyer's loan.
  • Sale without an agent: you save the agent fee and handle pricing, contracts and disclosures yourself.
  • Cash buyer: faster closing and no showings, with an offer that reflects repairs the buyer must pay for.

sections.h2: What does Greensboro look like to someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Greensboro is a large Piedmont city whose municipal site highlights downtown attractions such as the Steven Tanger Center for the Performing Arts, the Downtown Greenway, the Greensboro Science Center, Country Park and Lake Townsend. A free downtown hopper trolley also runs through the center of the city. Homes close to those amenities tend to be easier to explain to a buyer than houses far from them.

The city also publishes a lookup for council districts and a page of homes and property for sale that the city itself owns, which is separate from the private market. If your house sits in an older neighborhood, a rezoning question can arise: the city notes on its home page that rezoning could affect downtown property, so owners near the center should read the planning pages before setting a price.

sections.h2: Do short term rental rules in Greensboro affect what a buyer will pay?
sections.html:
Yes, because an investor who plans to use the house as a short term rental must obtain a city zoning permit first. The city defines a short term rental as a stay of 30 days or less.

The city's rules, as its short term rental page prints them, include these points:

  • Rentals are allowed only in residential dwelling units, and the permit must be posted inside the unit and in every listing.
  • No more than one dwelling unit, or 25 percent of the units in a multifamily building, may be used for short term rental.
  • Up to two adults are allowed per rented bedroom, and parking is limited to one car per bedroom rented.
  • Hosts of whole house rentals must be located in Guilford County or an adjacent county.

The page also states that the City Council removed the 750 foot setback between short term rentals at a February 18, 2025 meeting, and that this was the only change. Applications go through an online portal or in person at the Planner of the Day at City Hall. If you rent your own house this way today, tell a buyer whether the permit transfers; ask the city planning office rather than assuming it does.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 Guilford County reappraisal change for Greensboro sellers?
sections.html:
Guilford County's new real property values took effect January 1, 2026, and they appear on the tax bill that arrives in the summer of that year. The appeal deadline was May 15, 2026 at 5 p.m., and that window has closed.

The county explains that a reappraisal updates only the assessed value. Tax rates are set separately by elected boards each June for the fiscal year that begins July 1. County law requires a reappraisal at least every eight years, and Guilford carried out this one in house after the state Department of Revenue required it in April 2023 because homes were selling for more than their assessed values.

For a seller this matters in two ways. A buyer will look up your new assessed value, and a large jump from the 2022 figure can raise questions about the asking price. The county offers a sales comparison tool, an assessed value increase calculator and an online appeal platform. For questions, the county appraisal office lists 336-641-4814 and taxappraisal@guilfordcountync.gov.

sections.h2: What closing costs and taxes does a Greensboro seller face?
sections.html:
The main fixed charges are the deed excise tax and recording fees, and both are set by state law. The statute prints the excise rate as one dollar on each five hundred dollars, or fractional part, of the consideration, and it says the transferor pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

State charges that touch a Guilford County sale, as printed in the statutes
ItemWhat the statute saysSource
Deed excise tax$1.00 on each $500.00 or fractional part of the value conveyed; transferor pays before recordingG.S. 105-228.30
Recording a general instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 per additional pageG.S. 161-10
Property tax due dateSeptember 1; interest applies to payments on or after January 6G.S. 105-360

Unpaid property tax is a lien on the parcel, so the closing agent will ask for payoff figures. Ask the Guilford County tax office for the current balance on your parcel, since this page cannot show it.

sections.h2: What if the Greensboro house has a mortgage default, tenants or an inherited title?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own deadline, and a sale before the legal process ends can still be possible. In a North Carolina foreclosure the hearing is held before the clerk of superior court, and the notice of hearing must be served at least 10 days ahead.

  • Tenants: a month to month tenancy needs seven days' notice to quit, and a week to week tenancy needs two days, under G.S. 42-14.
  • Estates: an intestate small estate can be handled by affidavit if personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, but only after 30 days from the date of death.
  • Land contracts: a contract for deed for a one to four family home must be recorded, or a memorandum of it recorded, within five business days.

A seller who is behind on payments should call the loan servicer and the Guilford County Clerk of Superior Court early, and should ask a North Carolina attorney about the specific notice they received.

faqs.q: Who handles property taxes on a house in Greensboro?
faqs.a: Guilford County appraises the property and runs the tax office, which keeps counters in both Greensboro and High Point. Its appraisal office answers value questions at 336-641-4814. Tax rates are set each June by the elected boards.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Guilford County value?
faqs.a: No, the appeal deadline for the 2026 reappraisal was May 15, 2026 at 5 p.m., and the county posts that the period is closed. Later years follow the state appeal steps, which start with the county board of equalization and review and then the Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

faqs.q: Does a buyer need a permit to run a short term rental in Greensboro?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a zoning permit for rentals of 30 days or less, and the permit has to be displayed in the unit and in each listing. Applications can be filed through the city portal or in person at City Hall.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax when a Greensboro house sells?
faqs.a: The seller, who is the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The statute sets it at one dollar per five hundred dollars of consideration, or fractional part.

faqs.q: How soon can an heir sell an inherited Greensboro house?
faqs.a: It depends on how the title passes. A small estate affidavit may be filed 30 days after death when personal property less liens is within $20,000, and the affidavit lists each tract of real property. Larger estates need the clerk of superior court to appoint a personal representative; ask the clerk or an attorney.
